title: os
lede: Node-os-shaped operating-system information for portable CLI and microservice programs. The functions map onto real syscalls, /proc parsing and the Win32 APIs libuv itself uses rather than a fixed table, so os.cpus() returns live per-core tick counters, os.networkInterfaces() walks the real adapters, and os.release()/version() answer what Node answers on the same machine. os.cpus() speed reports the fixed 2400 MHz libuv nominal on Apple Silicon (where hw.cpufrequency is unavailable), cpufreq's scaling_max_freq or 0 on Linux (VMs and containers have no cpufreq), and Darwin times.irq is 0 — all exactly what real Node reports on that hardware; os.EOL is "\n" on POSIX hosts and "\r\n" on Windows.

entries.name: os.platform()
entries.description: Returns the operating-system platform string. Reuses process.platform's existing runtime.GOOS-constant mechanism, so the two always agree.

entries.name: os.homedir()
entries.description: Returns the current user's home directory, mirroring libuv's uv_os_homedir: a set HOME wins (an empty one included, matching Node's ""); on POSIX an unset HOME falls back to the passwd database (getpwuid), throwing a catchable Error only if that fails too. Windows reads USERPROFILE, falling back to the process token's profile directory.

entries.name: os.tmpdir()
entries.description: Returns the default temporary-file directory: on POSIX, process.env.TMPDIR (an unset or empty value falls back to "/tmp"), with a single trailing slash stripped unless the path is just "/". Never throws.

entries.name: os.hostname()
entries.description: Returns the host name of the operating system via POSIX gethostname().

entries.name: os.cpus()
entries.signature: cpus(): { model: string; speed: number; times: { user: number; nice: number; sys: number; idle: number; irq: number } }[]
entries.description: Returns real per-core {model, speed, times: {user, nice, sys, idle, irq}} objects — Linux via /proc/cpuinfo and /proc/stat parsing, Darwin via sysctlbyname and Mach host_processor_info — both verified (on Apple Silicon M4 Pro, model = "Apple M4 Pro" with live tick counters). On Apple Silicon, where hw.cpufrequency is unavailable, speed reports the fixed 2400 MHz nominal that real Node/libuv reports there; on Linux it reflects /proc/cpuinfo's current/scaled cpu MHz, matching real Node. Darwin times.irq is 0, exactly as real Node reports on Darwin.

entries.name: os.totalmem() / os.freemem()
entries.description: Return the total and free system memory in bytes. Verified on Linux and on Apple Silicon M4 Pro — totalmem() matches sysctl hw.memsize, and Darwin freemem() (Mach host_statistics) returns a live free-page figure.

returns.desc: Bytes of total or free memory.

entries.name: os.EOL
entries.description: The operating-system-specific end-of-line marker: "\r\n" on Windows, "\n" on POSIX, resolved as a compile-time constant of the build host (this compiler targets the host it runs on).

entries.name: os.type() / os.release() / os.version() / os.machine()
entries.signature: type(): string; release(): string; version(): string; machine(): string
entries.description: The uname-shaped identity strings. POSIX reads uname(); Windows reports "Windows_NT", RtlGetVersion's major.minor.build, the registry ProductName with libuv's "Windows 10" → "Windows 11" rewrite for build ≥ 22000, and x86_64/arm64 — verified byte-identical to Node on Windows 11.

entries.name: os.arch() / os.endianness() / os.devNull
entries.description: Compile-time constants of the build host, like process.arch: the Node architecture name ("x64", "arm64"), the byte order, and the null device ("\\\\.\\nul" on Windows, "/dev/null" elsewhere).

entries.name: os.uptime() / os.loadavg() / os.availableParallelism()
entries.signature: uptime(): number; loadavg(): number[]; availableParallelism(): number
entries.description: libuv's sources: seconds since boot as a double (CLOCK_BOOTTIME on Linux, kern.boottime on Darwin, GetTickCount64 on Windows); the 1/5/15-minute load averages via getloadavg, [0, 0, 0] on Windows as in Node; the CPUs this process may run on (the affinity set on Linux, the online count elsewhere, GetActiveProcessorCount on Windows), at least 1.

entries.name: os.userInfo()
entries.signature: userInfo(): { uid: number; gid: number; username: string; homedir: string; shell: string | null }
entries.description: The effective user's passwd entry on POSIX (uv_os_get_passwd); on Windows uid and gid are -1, username comes from GetUserNameW, homedir is os.homedir() and shell is null — exactly what Node reports. A failed lookup throws.
entries.snippet:
const u = os.userInfo();
console.log(u.username, u.homedir === os.homedir());

entries.name: os.networkInterfaces()
entries.description: An object keyed by interface name — a dynamic object, since the keys exist only at run time — each an array of { address, netmask, family, mac, internal, cidr, scopeid } records in libuv's order, with scopeid on IPv6 entries only. getifaddrs (up + running interfaces, MAC from the link-layer entry) on POSIX, GetAdaptersAddresses (operational adapters, FriendlyName, OnLinkPrefixLength) on Windows; cidr is null for a non-contiguous netmask. Verified byte-identical to Node's walk and JSON on Windows.
differences: Typed `any` rather than `NodeJS.Dict<NetworkInterfaceInfo[]>`: entries read through the dynamic paths (`for…of`, `Object.keys`, destructuring), so array methods on a per-interface list (`.filter`, `.map`) are the D1 method-through-`any` residue.
